inbox.subject: Final board numbers
inbox.body:
Alex,

Final numbers are in the deck, v7. ARR closes the reporting period at $17.8M. Burn multiple on the trailing quarter is 2.8x. Against the $19.0M year end plan we are forecasting a $1.2M gap.

The Harborline Mutual deal is not signed. I have it as pipeline only, not in the forecast, and the slide says so plainly. If it signs at $6 per employee per month across 40,000 employees it is about $2.9M of new ARR, but I would not let anyone round it in.

Happy to take the burn questions directly. See you at 7:30am.

Julian

inbox.subject: RE: Agreement status
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Quick update so you are not surprised. The agreement is still with our procurement and legal team, so it will not be signed this week. Diane is supportive and nothing substantive has come back on terms. Realistically we are looking at the first week of December for signature.

I will flag the moment it moves.

Best,
Celeste Navarro
Benefits Partnerships, Harborline Mutual

inbox.subject: Waves plan slide for today
inbox.body:
Alex,

I want to present the waves plan at the board today rather than a full launch. Wave one is 800 households on January 1, which is what our care leads can set up and still keep the promise. A full launch would put about 1,600 households into setup in January, and we do not have the capacity for that without breaking the Standing Plan windows.

Wave two picks up the remainder in February once the three Q1 care lead hires are ramped. Rehearsal at 9:15am if that still works.

Jordan

inbox.subject: VP of Care: two new leads
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Good week on the VP of Care search. We have two new leads: Maya Hollis, who ran home care operations for a regional health system, and Daniel Achterberg, currently head of member services at a senior living operator. Theo is still on for 5pm today after the board, and Maya can interview with you and Jordan next week.

I will bring both profiles to our 10:30am.

Best,
Grace Lindqvist
TalentBridge

inbox.subject: Brand campaign teaser
inbox.body:
Alex,

Feedback from Wednesday's session was strong across the room. Brand strategy looks good, and the employer panel responded well to the new line. I would like to tease the campaign at the board today, three slides at the end, nothing more than the direction and the launch window.

Draft is in the shared folder. Can review at 11:15am.

Tomás

inbox.subject: Donna's foot care appointment is confirmed
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Good news, Donna's foot care appointment is finally confirmed for Saturday at 10:30am with Dr. Hal Benning at Westbrook Foot and Ankle. It is the nail care and callus treatment plus her diabetic foot check that kept getting bumped.

I have booked the ride from her independent living residence and will meet her there. Tommy has the details in case anything changes on my side. I told Donna and she was relieved.

Erika

inbox.subject: Board logistics

Room 4B is booked from 1:30pm, video bridge tested. Two board members are joining remotely. Lunch for the room arrives at 1:45pm. I will send the locked PDF as soon as you sign off at noon.

Marisol

inbox.subject: See you at 2

Alex,

I will be in the room at 2. Looking forward to the January plan discussion. Could you leave ten minutes at the end for executive session?

Helen

newsletters.title: Employers lean into caregiving benefits for 2027
newsletters.body: Benefits buyers report caregiving support as a top three request in open enrollment surveys. Several mid-size insurers are piloting per-employee caregiving programs, with procurement cycles running longer than expected into December.

newsletters.title: Staging launches without breaking service
newsletters.body: A look at phased rollouts across service businesses. Operators who launched in waves reported fewer missed commitments in the first 60 days than those who launched all at once.
